It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the "unsearchable riches" of Christ while witnessing a world where many young men are "tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine," and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the drawing of men toward or away from God in this hour? [13, 419, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling "overwhelmed and desperate" because you see a generation "infatuated with the world" and "choked with cares, riches, and pleasures," or are you seeking a "settled certainty" to anchor your soul in the truth that "God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation"—including the hearts of men? [13, 20, 188, 298, 1143, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many "shave off the edges" of the truth to offer "spiritual placebos" that "cater to people’s itching ears," we must return to the "external Word" to see how the Lord personally governs the "vicissitudes of life" by demanding that we "rightly divide the word of truth" [11, 28, 477, 766, 1503, 1515, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that "unbelief is the seed" of every departure from God, and therefore, a young man's drift into "practical humanism" is not an "administrative anomaly" but evidence of a "rebellious heart" that God uses to prove that "His counsel shall stand, and He will do all His pleasure" (Isaiah 46:10) [1, 9, 15, 68, 1143, 1388, 1456, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Source of the Drift (Why Men Turn Away)**

**Verse**
“ ‘Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world—the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life—is not of the Father but is of the world’ ” (1 John 2:15–16). [765, 822, 1569, 1570, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Scripture reveals that men are drawn away because "men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil" (John 3:19) [11, 62, 1131, 1406, 1443, 1460, 1515, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham**—notes that the "world" is an "invisible spiritual system of evil dominated by Satan" that appeals to a young man's "passions, vision, and pride" [765, 1391, 1573, 1585, Conversation History]. Because "the carnal mind is enmity against God," a young man who "trusts in his own heart" is a "fool" who will find that his "achievement, insights, and wisdom" lead only to being "wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked" (Romans 8:7; Proverbs 28:26; Revelation 3:17) [65, 196, 212, 303, 341, 1151, 1313, 1388, 1500, 1523, 1531, 1555, Conversation History]. 

**Takeaway**
You should "not be deceived" by "worldly philosophies" that promise "self-satisfaction," for "your life is not your own" because you were "bought at a price" (1 Corinthians 6:19–20; Colossians 2:8) [12, 91, 101, 257, 312, 1138, 1231, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1524, 1670, Conversation History]. You must "discipline your body and bring it into subjection," recognizing that "if anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him" (1 Corinthians 9:27; 1 John 2:15) [13, 20, 79, 116, 280, 297, 765, 873, 1054, 1058, 1313, 1406, 1503, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the "religious leaders" relied on "lineage and circumcision" to define their standing, yet Jesus exposed them as being "of your father the devil" because they did not "abide in My word" (John 8:31, 44) [22, 151, 185, 203, 922, 1201, 1352, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that "the true circumcision" is "that of the heart, in the Spirit," meaning that no amount of "rabbinic tradition" or "ritualized ceremonies" can replace the need for "the washing of regeneration" (Romans 2:29; Titus 3:5) [13, 24, 142, 358, 410, 802, 842, 846, 1104, 1214, 1313, 1426, 1445, 1529, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Divine Draw (Why Men Turn Toward God)**

**Verse**
“ ‘No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him; and I will raise him up at the last day’ ” (John 6:44). [202, 345, 824, 1277, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The sources teach that "salvation is a supernatural work of God," where the Holy Spirit "opens the sinner’s heart to receive the message" [11, 251, 280, 339, 344, 429, 557, 561, 803, 822, 1091, Conversation History]. A young man is drawn to God not by "human ingenuity" or "seeker-friendly" methods, but because the Spirit "convicts the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment" (John 16:8) [32, 114, 197, 281, 392, 457, 471, 551, 654, 712, 1530, Conversation History]. God often uses "suffering" and "various trials" as a "verbal cudgel" to "peel away the flesh and drive you to Himself," for "the testing of your faith produces endurance" (James 1:3; 2 Thessalonians 1:5) [13, 31, 68, 80, 131, 300, 321, 365, 784, 886, 1012, 1111, 1313, 1408, 1515, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Trade in your worry for trust," knowing that "He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ" (Philippians 1:6) [5, 94, 201, 356, 442, 630, 829, 1040, 1132, 1143, 1408, 1515, 1572, Conversation History]. You should "not look for some other fountain of knowledge" in "cleverly devised myths," but instead "tremble at My word," for "faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God" (Isaiah 66:2; Romans 10:17; 2 Peter 1:16) [11, 36, 51, 101, 116, 123, 240, 282, 478, 521, 764, 785, 855, 1313, 1334, 1406, 1503, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, "temporal signs" like "national greatness" and "large cities" were used to show God's favor, but the "true Jew" was still the one who would "circumcise the foreskin of your heart" (Deuteronomy 10:16; 28:1) [409, 500, 755, 800, 802, 934, 1214, 1313, 1342, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our "victory," teaching that we are "sojourners and pilgrims" whose "citizenship is in heaven," and we "conquer" not through "carnal weaponry" but "by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony" (Philippians 3:20; 1 Peter 2:11; Revelation 12:11) [13, 21, 26, 32, 38, 92, 142, 440, 1113, 1203, 1223, 1259, 1313, 1402, 1426, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

### **Section 3: Biblical Patterns of Masculine Spiritual Formation**

**Verse**
“ ‘Watch, stand fast in the faith, be brave, be strong. Let all that you do be done with love’ ” (1 Corinthians 16:13–14). [169, 1056, 1057, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that "Jesus’ definition of leadership is one of self-sacrificing service," and to "empower women" at the expense of "divine order" is a "divine judgment on a nation" [102, 150, 159, 160, 1399, Conversation History]. True masculine formation requires that a man "deny himself, and take up his cross daily" to follow a Master who "stooped all the way down" and "took upon Himself the form of a servant" (Luke 9:23; Philippians 2:7) [31, 102, 199, 207, 362, 737, 759, 773, 868, 911, 981, 1132, 1231, 1232, 1233, 1406, Conversation History]. As a "slave of Christ," the young man’s "sole objective" is to be a "vessel for honor, sanctified and useful for the Master," which involves "training up a child in the way he should go" and "loving your own wife as your own body" (2 Timothy 2:21; Proverbs 22:6; Ephesians 5:28) [12, 101, 312, 335, 361, 462, 593, 693, 803, 810, 863, 1148, 1166, 1257, 1406, 1432, 1450, 1670, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Never become so involved in this world" that you seek a "platform for your own ego," for you are called to "lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity" (1 Timothy 2:2) [21, 51, 77, 82, 87, 125, 130, 925, 1105, 1110, 1201, 1284, 1503, 1515, 1623, Conversation History]. You must "discipline your mind" to "dwell on whatever things are true, whatever things are noble," refusing to "ape the world’s fads" of "sensual talk and carnal conduct" (Philippians 4:8) [11, 35, 76, 101, 116, 132, 138, 139, 141, 143, 212, 294, 361, 444, 457, 458, 461, 462, 467, 469, 581, 601, 604, 617, 718, 774, 775, 831, 832, 873, 917, 918, 919, 982, 1013, 1017, 1022, 1024, 1050, 1054, 1058, 1110, 1121, 1125, 1138, 1141, 1143, 1225, 1242, 1246, 1247, 1251, 1252, 1253, 1254, 1257, 1262, 1269, 1284, 1289, 1313, 1315, 1316, 1320, 1342, 1402, 1403, 1406, 1407, 1408, 1414, 1426, 1429, 1431, 1432, 1440, 1441, 1450, 1461, 1462, 1466, 1468, 1471, 1473, 1479, 1484, 1488, 1490, 1502, 1503, 1506, 1507, 1512, 1513, 1515, 1523, 1524, 1527, 1528, 1530, 1532, 1534, 1535, 1536, 1540, 1542, 1544, 1545, 1547, 1548, 1549, 1550, 1551, 1554, 1555, 1556, 1560, 1563, 1564, 1567, 1572, 1573, 1574, 1576, 1577, 1580, 1581, 1583, 1585, 1586, 1587, 1592, 1594, 1595, 1596, 1597, 1601, 1605, 1611, 1613, 1614, 1616, 1617, 1622, 1634, 1636, 1638, 1642, 1646, 1649, 1653, 1662, 1664, 1665, 1666, 1667, 1670, 1672, 1675, 1680, 1684, 1692, 1694, 1702, 1709, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual vs. Reality**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, "the older shall serve the younger" was contrary to custom, but God declared it to show that "His sovereign elective purposes did not necessarily have to follow custom" (Genesis 25:23) [790, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the "pattern," revealing that "everything the Sabbath signified has been completely fulfilled in the finished work of Christ," meaning we are no longer bound by "ritualized ceremonies" but by "the renewing of your mind" to "prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God" (Romans 12:1–2; Hebrews 4:10) [13, 17, 24, 136, 137, 142, 157, 446, 490, 491, 595, 596, 611, 651, 652, 661, 755, 761, 776, 831, 860, 876, 1101, 1212, 1313, 1426, 1445, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: Reverence The Old Testament saints didn’t flippantly rush into God’s presence, treating Him as if He were a man. They came before Him with reverence, recognizing that when they prayed, they were coming face-to-face with Almighty God. The prophet Isaiah saw the Lord in a vision “sitting on a throne, lofty and exalted, with the train of His robe filling the temple” (6:1). His response was, “I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts” (v. 5).

system that is the enemy of God, we are not to see those in it as our personal enemies. They are captives of the real enemy, the devil (cf. 2 Tim. 2:24–26). They are not our enemies; they are our mission field. The Presence of Holiness To promote a “tranquil and quiet life,” believers must pursue “godliness and dignity.” Godliness translates “eusebeia,” a common word in the Pastoral Epistles. It carries the idea of reverence toward God. Believers should live for the majesty, holiness, love, and glory of God.
